evidence.source: 李學勤主編, 字源, 2012, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社; direct inspection of original scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0684/source.png
evidence.field: 病 entry; PDF p. 684, printed p. 671; headword, graphic labels, formation and meaning discussion inspected; following PDF p. 685 checked for continuation
evidence.text: The scan labels the entry 病 bìng and prints “形声字。从疒,丙声(或从方声)”; later it says “本义是重病” and quotes Shuowen “病,疾加也。从疒,丙声,” glossing 疾加 as illness worsening. It lists diagrams labeled Warring States, Shuowen small seal, Qin, Han and clerical. The entry ends on printed p. 671; p. 672 begins another entry, with no 病 continuation. The book therefore attributes both 丙 and 方 sound analyses, but the prose and labels do not establish which depicted occurrence supports 方. The printed page number and these text spans were read from the scan pixels. The OCR corpus text inspected matches the scan for the relevant passage; no correction is proposed.
evidence.title: 字源

evidence.source: 台灣教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.field: 說文釋形, Mandarin reading and attested dictionary senses
evidence.text: The entry gives the received Shuowen wording “疾加也。从疒，丙聲” and Mandarin bìng. It records noun, verb and adjective senses: illness, being troubled, concern, harm, resentment, criticism, withered foliage and fatigue. These dictionary examples support the existence of varied uses but do not by themselves provide a complete semantic chronology.
evidence.title: A02667 病 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 劉殿爵, 「疾」與「病」, CUHK Chinese Language and Literature Research Centre
evidence.field: interpretation of 疾加也 and early transmitted word senses
evidence.text: Liu reads 疾加 as a dynamic worsening of illness, distinguishing that gloss from a static “serious illness” interpretation. He analyzes pre-Qin uses of 病 as verbal or adjectival meanings such as trouble, hardship, harm, worry and distress, and argues that noun “illness/serious illness” arose later. This is an attributed scholarly proposal based on transmitted texts, not direct evidence for the earliest physical graph.
evidence.title: 「疾」與「病」

evidence.source: 中国辞书学报第三辑, article on 病 word history, PDF pp. 4–7
evidence.text: The article argues that in seven transmitted pre-Qin works 病 appears with verbal and adjectival uses but not as a noun meaning disease or serious illness; it places noun disease uses after the Warring States period. It also says 病 is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and proposes “困苦” (hardship) as its original word meaning. These are the author's claims and deductions; the inspected passage does not establish an artifact-level first graph attestation. This differs from 字源's proposal “本义是重病” and from Liu's interpretation of Shuowen's gloss, so the accounts should remain attributed rather than harmonized.
evidence.title: 中国辞书学报第三辑

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, online transcription and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 病 entry, 卷七 疒部
evidence.text: The inspected transcription reads “病，疾加也。从疒丙聲.” Duan Yucai's note assigns the old sound to his tenth rhyme division. This is the received dictionary explanation and does not establish the graph's earliest construction.

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, version 1.1 table (2014); table values surfaced in search result; Oxford Academic book record inspected

evidence.text: The searchable table gives 病 *[b]raŋ-s and 丙 *praŋʔ. These are reconstructions, not attested ancient pronunciations, and show shared rhyme and substantial segmental material with differences in onset specification and suffix. The PDF itself could not be opened during this inspection; do not treat its search-result transcription as direct table-page inspection.

gaps: The 字源 passage directly supports an attributed alternative 从方声, but does not tie 方 to a specific labeled historical specimen. Keep its occurrence-level graphic basis unresolved and do not assert 方 as an established component.

The article in 中国辞书学报 argues 病 is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and places noun disease uses after the Warring States, but its inspected discussion does not establish the earliest physical 病 artifact or precise date.

字源's proposal that 病 originally meant serious illness, Shuowen's 疾加也 gloss, and the contrasting hardship-origin proposal in the inspected article are distinct source claims. Liu's dynamic-worsening interpretation adds a further account; no synthesis resolving them was found.
The Baxter–Sagart PDF table was not directly opened. Its values came from a search result; the Oxford Academic record verifies book authorship/publication but not these character-specific readings.

Official Unicode Unihan pages for U+4E19 and U+75C5 could not be opened. Local kMandarin rows were checked; current readings are available from Taiwan CNS entries, but official Unihan click-through verification remains outstanding.

No new OCR error was found in 字源 PDF p. 684: the scanned text “形声字。从疒,丙声(或从方声)” and “本义是重病” matches the provisional corpus transcription. The scan shows labeled forms for Warring States, Shuowen small seal, Qin, Han and clerical; this report preserves the current glyph selection and makes no image-candidate recommendation.
